### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. complement component 3 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.467)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-198933, Reactome:R-HSA-977606)

**Proposed mechanism:** CD81 (HGNC:2377) —DISRUPTS→ Complement System Activation (GO:0006955); Complement System Activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002717); C3 (HGNC:1704) —DISRUPTS→ Complement System Activation (GO:0006955); Complement System Activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002717). Loss of function in CD81 (a regulator of the complement system) and C3 (a central effector of the complement system) both lead to impaired complement activation, resulting in increased susceptibility to recurrent bacterial infections.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of impaired complement system activation, as measured by CH50 or other complement assays, in individuals with CD81 deficiency would falsify this hypothesis. Conversely, finding normal complement function in C3 deficient individuals would also falsify it. _(variant: rs747771634)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream impact of CD81 and C3 on the complement system may reveal therapeutic targets for recurrent infections in both conditions, potentially involving complement modulators.

#### 2. obsolete blood group system, landsteiner-wiener  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.277)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-198933)

**Proposed mechanism:** CD81 (HGNC:2373) —BINDS→ Leukocyte adhesion and migration (GO:0050900); ICAM4 (HGNC:4997) —BINDS→ Leukocyte adhesion and migration (GO:0050900); Leukocyte adhesion and migration (GO:0050900) —LEADS_TO→ Regulation of immune response (GO:0050776); Leukocyte adhesion and migration (GO:0050900) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal erythrocyte morphology (HP:0004465); Regulation of immune response (GO:0050776) —LEADS_TO→ Altered red blood cell surface antigen expression (HP:0030074). Mutations in CD81 and ICAM4, both involved in leukocyte adhesion and migration, can disrupt these processes. This disruption may lead to altered immune responses and consequently affect erythrocyte morphology and surface antigen expression, linking the two diseases through shared pathways.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that CD81 and ICAM4 function in entirely independent cellular processes with no downstream overlap in cellular signaling or phenotype, or identification of disease-specific variants in CD81 and ICAM4 that do not affect shared pathways. _(variant: rs743268369)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular mechanisms involving CD81 and ICAM4 could lead to therapeutic strategies that target common pathways to treat aspects of both diseases, such as by modulating immune cell interactions or erythrocyte surface properties.
